elena: Heads up: seeing increased gRPC stream stalls through the edge in eu-west-1 — clients hang for a while then get resets. Not model CPU. Anyone else seeing this?

aj: Yep. p95 for streaming endpoints jumps to ~12s then we see `grpc-status=14` and occasional GOAWAY from the edge. Seems correlated with bursts of short-lived streams. Suspect idle timeout + connection pooling oddness.

kai: Concrete signal: ALB/edge logs show a lot of connection reuse via the same NAT egress IPs. We're hitting ephemeral port pressure and connections get queued at the proxy. Also saw repeated `WINDOW_UPDATE` in the h2 trace but no DATA flow after that. Uploading tcpdump next.

elena: Stack is edge Envoy -> ALB -> per-pod sidecar (Envoy) -> service. Some traffic path takes a shared NAT gateway. My theory: connection pooling + port exhaustion -> downstream stalls that surface as h2 stream timeouts/resets.

sofia: Quick canary: I bumped edge Envoy `idle_timeout` 60s -> 120s on canary ALB, and increased `http2_protocol_options.max_concurrent_streams` from 16 -> 100 for streaming routes. Rolling monitor now.

infra-ops: FYI, NAT ephemeral ports per egress IP are ~65k but TIME_WAIT and ephemeral range reduce effective available ports. For lots of short TCP connections (which our streaming clients sometimes create) you can exhaust usable ports quickly. Short-term mitigation: allocate more egress IPs for eu-west-1 (rg-2).

aj: Repro tips: `tcpdump -nn -s0 -w /tmp/h2.pcap port 443 and host <edge-ip>`, then `grpcurl -proto x.proto -d '{}' -H 'te: trailers' <edge-host>` to nail a streaming session. Look for `RST_STREAM` and `GOAWAY` in the capture. Also check Envoy logs for `stream reset, reason: connection termination`.

kai: Observed buffering behavior: clients block (~several seconds), then a burst of tokens/data. Could be an H2 flow-control bug in our Envoy (we're on 1.23). There's a known fix in 1.25 for flow-control/window update races when proxy-chaining.

elena: Proposed plan: 1) add 4 extra egress IPs to eu-west-1 gateway temporarily, 2) canary Envoy upgrade to 1.25 on a subset of edge nodes, 3) tune `idle_timeout` and `max_concurrent_streams` for streaming routes, 4) if still bad, route streaming traffic to a dedicated pool with dedicated egress (no shared NAT). Who can own egress IPs?

infra-ops: I'll take the egress IPs (tracking RG-143). ETA ~30m to allocate and push routing. Also will widen kernel ephemeral range on the gateways from `32768-60999` -> `1024-65535` and reduce `TIME_WAIT` via `tcp_tw_reuse` where safe.

sofia: :thumbsup: I'll run the Envoy canary upgrade after smoke tests. If the canary fixes flow-control we can promote. Otherwise we flip to dedicated pool routing for heavy streaming customers.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457 edge-streaming-egress. Pager duty has been notified and runbook link added: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-streaming-egress

elena: Thanks all — please paste relevant logs/pcaps in this thread as you have them. If anybody sees a specific client user impact spike, post the customer id so we can prioritize rerouting.
